name: Zoutleeuw, c. 1650
attribution: Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); historical land cover, town walls and gates from the Ferraris map (1777) and the Villaret map (1745-48), Digitaal Vlaanderen (geo.api.vlaanderen.be/HISTCART)

gateSources.Sint-Truidensepoort: inventory 140044 (barbican from 1642); Ferraris 'Porte de St Tron'
gateSources.Westpoort: unlabelled/illegible Ferraris gate on the west side; name is a placeholder

walls.source: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Zoutleeuw' (https://id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140044)
walls.note: Zoutleeuw third wall (from 1552, taking in the second wall of c. 1300) with five gates, repaired and given half-moons and hornworks from 1642; traced from the Ferraris map (1777). The citadel south of the town dates from 1670-79 and is NOT included.

landmarks.y1650: Gothic collegiate church, its interior untouched by the iconoclasm of 1566 (the only one in the Low Countries), with the stone sacrament tower of Cornelis Floris (1550-52). The great west tower was never built.
Town hall of 1538-39 by Rombout Keldermans.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Zoutleeuw' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140044)

landmarks.y1650: Cloth hall of 1316, built on the wall of the first enceinte; tower of the old Sint-Truidensepoort beside it.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Zoutleeuw' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140044)

landmarks.y1650: Beguinage moved to its present site after 1578.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Zoutleeuw' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140044)

ruler.name: Hertogdom Brabant
ruler.sovereign: Philip IV of Spain, as duke (Spanish Netherlands); governor Archduke Leopold Wilhelm 1647-56
ruler.source: nl.wikipedia 'Hertogdom Brabant'; Vrede van Munster (1648); inventory 140194 (Halen); docs/research/history-check.md F31 (governor)
